generic_sampling_rules.int_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL; never overwritten by shaping passes.
generic_sampling_rules.int_fk: Sample from the parent table's generated primary-key pool; allow NULL only if the column is nullable; never overwritten with non-key placeholders.
generic_sampling_rules.int_quantity: Integer in [1, 200]; occasionally 0 or negative only if a range rule allows it.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Pick from a small pool of realistic names; allow near-duplicates (case/whitespace variants) and occasional NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Pick uniformly from the enum values listed in per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.text_time: Format 'HH:MM' with HH in 00-23 and MM in 00-59.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Short realistic phrase; allow near-duplicates and occasional NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, generate L-0.001, L, L+0.001 (or integer step 1 for INT).
generic_sampling_rules.tie_order: Ensure at least two rows share the tie value at the listed rank.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, ~10% NULL rows per instance, at least one NULL row; NOT NULL columns never get NULL; planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule.

per_column_exceptions.targets: station.Station_ID, station.Name, station.Location, station.Main_Services, station.Number_of_Platforms, train_station.Station_ID
per_column_exceptions.rule: Ensure group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 occur when grouping by these columns. Shape by repeating actual values from the column's own domain (integer key values for INT columns, pool values for text columns); never inject string placeholders into INT columns and never overwrite PK/FK values with values outside the parent key pool.
Include parent rows with no child rows and child rows whose FK matches a parent; no NULL FKs (NOT NULL columns).
Ensure COUNT(*) and COUNT(col) values 1, 2, 3 occur across groups; shape by repeating actual key/pool values, not synthetic placeholders.

per_column_exceptions.targets: train_station.Station_ID, station.Name, station.Location, station.Annual_interchanges, station.Main_Services, train.Time
per_column_exceptions.rule: Create ties at rank 1 for DESC/ASC orderings on the listed aggregates/columns; for train.Time ensure at least two rows share the earliest time (LIMIT 100 tie is relaxed to match the 11-row table size).
20-50% duplicate share on DISTINCT columns; for train_station.Train_ID duplicate only across rows with distinct Station_ID so the composite PK stays unique.

Include values 24.999, 25, 25.001 for Annual_entry_exit; 8.999, 9, 9.001, 24.999, 25, 25.001 for Total_Passengers. Negative literals (-21.001, -21, -20.999) are dropped because Total_Passengers >= 0 and equals a sum of non-negatives; the formula rule takes precedence over boundary planting.
Column is NOT NULL; no NULL rows generated.

supporting_evidence.Total_Passengers formula: station rows 1-8 show Total_Passengers = Annual_entry_exit + Annual_interchanges within rounding.
supporting_evidence.Total_Passengers NULL handling: Total_Passengers is nullable; when either operand is NULL the formula is not applied (SQL three-valued logic) and the row keeps its NULL.

generation_specification.uncertainty: Location values in sample include 'Glasgow' not matching station names; treated as independent free text with no correlation to Name. Main_Services free text. Train.Name duplicates allowed. The train.Time LIMIT 100 tie is relaxed to two rows because the table has only 11 rows.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations: 184 across 20 instances (all 20 invalid due to new_integrity_failures). The generator's _apply_aggregate_counts (instance.py) overwrites train_station.Station_ID with synthetic string values 'S1','S2','S3','S100'... after fill_foreign_keys_consistently has already drawn valid FK values from station.Station_ID. These synthetic values never match any station.Station_ID, so every generated train_station row violates the FK to station. Similarly _apply_group_sizes overwrites station.Station_ID (and other columns) with 'G1','G2','G3','U%d' strings, breaking the parent key pool that train_station FKs must reference. The writer disables foreign_keys pragma (writer.py: 'pragma foreign_keys = OFF'), so violations are silently committed.
issues.requested_revision: Do not overwrite FK/PK columns with synthetic placeholder strings. Shape group sizes / aggregate counts by choosing values from the actual parent key pool (e.g. pick a subset of station.Station_ID values and repeat them to create group sizes 1/2/>=3), and shape train_station.Station_ID only from values present in station.Station_ID. Ensure the FK-consistency pass runs after all shaping, or re-validate FKs before writing. Keep foreign_keys enforcement on (or verify FK integrity) so violations are caught.

issues.evidence: The spec's null_rows target is train_station.Station_ID with rule 'Column is NOT NULL; no NULL rows generated.' The program's _plant_nulls plants NULLs on every nullable column, and the execution feedback shows NULLs generated in station.Name (10/109), station.Location (14/109), station.Main_Services (11/109), station.Number_of_Platforms (12/109), train.Name (6/29), train.Service (3/29), train.Time (3/29). Per the interface NULL rule this is acceptable for nullable columns, but the spec's null_targets list only names train_station.Station_ID and does not enumerate the other nullable columns; the spec should be reconciled with the interface rule. More importantly, station.Total_Passengers shows NULL 0/109 despite being nullable — the formula re-application after NULL planting (_apply_formula) skips rows where operands are NULL, leaving Total_Passengers non-NULL, which is fine, but the spec should state the intended NULL behavior for Total_Passengers explicitly.
issues.requested_revision: Update the specification's null_targets / null rule to enumerate all nullable columns and their intended NULL share (matching the interface rule), and confirm Total_Passengers NULL handling. No code change strictly required for nullable columns, but the spec must be consistent with the interface NULL rule.

issues.evidence: The spec's semantic rule 'Total_Passengers = Annual_entry_exit + Annual_interchanges' is supported by evidence from rows 1-8 only (supporting_evidence cites 8 rows). The spec also lists comparison_boundary literals for Total_Passengers including negative values (-21.001, -21, -20.999) and 8.999/9/9.001, but the semantic range rule requires Total_Passengers >= 0 and the formula requires it to equal the sum of two non-negative columns. Planting -21.001/-21/-20.999 into Total_Passengers (via _apply_boundaries) then re-applying the formula overwrites them, so the negative boundary literals are never actually present in the data — the boundary rule and the formula rule conflict. The spec does not resolve this conflict.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the comparison_boundary literals for Total_Passengers with the formula and range rules: either drop the negative literals (since Total_Passengers >= 0 and equals a sum of non-negatives), or specify that boundary literals apply only to Annual_entry_exit/Annual_interchanges. Document which rule takes precedence.

issues.evidence: The spec's ties_for_order_limit for train.Time requires 'at least 100 rows share the earliest time when LIMIT 100 is applied', but table_sizes_per_instance sets train to 11 rows. _apply_ties sets min(n, TIME_LIMIT_TIE)=11 rows to '00:00', so at most 11 rows share the earliest time — the 100-row tie is impossible with 11 train rows. The spec is internally inconsistent (table size 11 vs. tie requirement of 100).
issues.requested_revision: Either increase train table size to >= 100 (and update table_sizes_per_instance), or relax the train.Time tie requirement to match the table size. The spec must be self-consistent.

issues.evidence: The spec's group_sizes target includes station.Station_ID, station.Name, station.Location, station.Main_Services, station.Number_of_Platforms, train_station.Station_ID. _apply_group_sizes overwrites these with 'G1','G2','G3','U%d' strings, which for station.Station_ID (INT PK) and train_station.Station_ID (INT FK) produces non-integer values and breaks FK integrity (see issue 1). For station.Name/Location/Main_Services the overwrite also destroys the text pools and near-duplicate logic applied earlier, and for Number_of_Platforms (INT) it produces strings. The group-size shaping is applied to columns where it is semantically invalid.
issues.requested_revision: Restrict group-size shaping to columns where it is type-appropriate and does not break keys: for station.Station_ID and train_station.Station_ID, shape by repeating actual integer key values from the parent pool; for text columns, shape by repeating pool values; for Number_of_Platforms, use integer values. Do not inject string placeholders into INT columns.

issues.evidence: The spec's duplicates_for_distinct target includes train_station.Train_ID with 20-50% duplicate share. _apply_distinct_duplicates copies values from other rows, but train_station.Train_ID is part of the composite PK (Train_ID, Station_ID). Duplicating Train_ID across rows with distinct Station_ID is fine for the PK, but combined with _apply_aggregate_counts overwriting Station_ID with 'S1'..'S3' placeholders, the composite PK may collide or the FK breaks. The execution feedback shows pk_duplicates: 0, so PK is currently safe, but the interaction is fragile and the FK violation (issue 1) is the concrete failure.
issues.requested_revision: After all shaping, re-run sample_fresh_primary_keys and FK re-validation on train_station to guarantee both PK uniqueness and FK validity. Document the ordering of shaping passes so PK/FK constraints are preserved.

issues.evidence: The spec's uncertainty note says 'Location values in sample include Glasgow not matching station names; treated as free text.' The program's LOCATION_POOL = ['London','Birmingham','Glasgow'] and NAME_POOL includes 'Glasgow Central'. This is consistent with the free-text treatment, but the spec does not state whether Location should correlate with Name. No evidence of a rule requiring correlation, so this is a minor documentation gap rather than an error.
issues.requested_revision: Optionally document that Location is independent free text (no correlation with Name) to remove ambiguity.

unresolved_checks: Whether the compact database's actual NULL share per nullable column matches the program's NULL_SHARE=0.10; the feedback shows generated-row NULL counts but not the compact share, so the 'follow the compact database's share' part of the interface rule cannot be fully verified.

Whether the 23/72 separated construction pairs are sufficient for value variation; the feedback does not break down which patterns separated, so it is unclear whether the FK-violation issue is masking intended separations.
Whether station.Total_Passengers NULL 0/109 is intended given the formula re-application; the spec does not state the intended NULL behavior for this column.

issues.evidence: The specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas include Total_Passengers = Annual_entry_exit + Annual_interchanges (evidence from rows 1-8), and the program implements this in _apply_formula (instance.py) with round(x+y,3) and tolerance 0.01. The formula is applied only when both operands and the destination are non-NULL, consistent with SQL three-valued logic and the NULL rule. The negative boundary literals (-21.001, -21, -20.999) for Total_Passengers are explicitly dropped in spec.py BOUNDARIES with a documented rationale (formula precedence over boundary planting). This is a defensible design decision, not an error.
issues.requested_revision: None required. Optionally document in the spec that the formula rule takes precedence over the negative boundary literals for Total_Passengers, which is already stated in the per_column_exceptions.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule requires ~10% NULL share per nullable column and at least one NULL row. Execution feedback shows generated NULL counts: station.Annual_entry_exit 9/53, Annual_interchanges 5/53, Location 6/53, Main_Services 4/53, Name 8/53, Number_of_Platforms 7/53, Total_Passengers 9/53, train.Name 6/29, train.Service 2/29, train.Time 5/29. All nullable columns have at least one NULL and non-NULL values. The share is computed against the appended generated rows (n per instance), and _plant_nulls uses max(1, round(0.10*n)). This satisfies the interface NULL rule. Note: the share is measured against generated rows only, not the full table including compact rows; this is consistent with the 'generated rows' framing in the feedback.
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's group_sizes and aggregate_boundary shaping rules require sizes 1, 2, >=3 and COUNT values 1, 2, 3. The program's _shape_group_sizes and _apply_aggregate_counts use a fixed plan [g1, g2, g2, g3, g3, g3] for the first 6 rows, then append base[i%len(base)]+1000+i for the rest. For train_station (11 rows) this yields group sizes 1, 2, 3 for Station_ID, satisfying the target. However, the plan is deterministic in structure (only the base values vary), so the 'variation' across instances is limited to the choice of base values. This is acceptable for the stated targets but reduces diversity. Not a blocking error.
issues.requested_revision: None required for pass. Optional improvement: randomize the group-size plan (e.g., shuffle which rows get which group size) to increase instance diversity.

issues.evidence: The specification's ties_for_order_limit for train.Time is relaxed to TIME_LIMIT_TIE=2 (documented in spec.py and uncertainty). _apply_ties sets the first 2 rows to '00:00' and randomizes the rest. This satisfies the relaxed tie requirement. The original target was LIMIT(100) tie at rank 100, which is impossible with 11 rows; the relaxation is explicitly justified in the specification's uncertainty field.
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's duplicates_for_distinct requires 20-50% duplicate share on station.Name, train_station.Train_ID, train.Name. _apply_distinct_duplicates implements this by copying values from random other rows. For train_station.Train_ID, the rule states duplicates only across rows with distinct Station_ID so the composite PK stays unique. The program's _apply_distinct_duplicates does not explicitly check Station_ID distinctness when duplicating Train_ID; however, sample_fresh_primary_keys is called after shaping (in build_random_instance) and drops rows with duplicate (Train_ID, Station_ID) tuples, so composite PK uniqueness is preserved. The duplicate share may be reduced by this dedup, but the integrity check confirms pk_duplicates=0 across 20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: None required. The post-shaping PK dedup compensates for the lack of explicit Station_ID-distinctness in the duplicate pass.

issues.evidence: The specification's unmatched_join_rows requires parent rows with no child rows and child rows whose FK matches a parent, with no NULL FKs. _apply_unmatched is a no-op (returns immediately), relying on the child plan using only a subset of parent keys. With station=12, train=11, train_station=11, and _apply_aggregate_counts shaping Station_ID to use only 3 base values (plus 1000+i offsets for rows 6-10), the child rows reference a small subset of station keys, leaving many station rows unmatched. Similarly for train. The execution feedback shows fk_violations=0, confirming FK consistency. The unmatched-parent condition is satisfied by construction (12 stations, 11 child rows using ~3-5 distinct station keys).
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's comparison_boundary requires values 24.999, 25, 25.001 for Annual_entry_exit and 8.999, 9, 9.001, 24.999, 25, 25.001 for Total_Passengers. _apply_boundaries plants these literals at the first positions of the column. However, _apply_formula runs after _apply_boundaries and overwrites Total_Passengers with Annual_entry_exit + Annual_interchanges for non-NULL rows. This means the planted boundary values 8.999, 9, 9.001, 24.999, 25, 25.001 in Total_Passengers are overwritten by the formula, so the boundary values do not survive in the final data. The specification's per_column_exceptions states 'the formula rule takes precedence over boundary planting' for the negative literals, but does not explicitly state that the positive boundary literals are also overwritten. This is a minor inconsistency: the boundary planting for Total_Passengers is effectively a no-op for non-NULL rows.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: either (a) apply boundaries after the formula for Total_Passengers (but then the formula would be violated), or (b) document in spec.py that Total_Passengers boundary planting is superseded by the formula for all non-NULL rows, and rely on Annual_entry_exit boundaries to produce Total_Passengers values near 25 via the formula (e.g., Annual_entry_exit=25, Annual_interchanges=0 gives Total_Passengers=25). Option (b) is cleaner and consistent with the formula-precedence principle. This is a documentation/clarity issue, not a blocking error, since the formula is the stronger semantic rule.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_targets lists station.Name, Annual_entry_exit, Annual_interchanges, Total_Passengers, Location, Main_Services, Number_of_Platforms, train.Name, train.Time, train.Service. The program's _plant_nulls iterates over tm.columns and plants NULLs for all nullable columns (not just the listed null_targets). This is broader than the specification's null_targets list but consistent with the interface NULL rule ('for every nullable column'). The execution feedback confirms NULLs in all 10 listed columns. No NOT NULL column receives NULL (integrity check not_null_violations=0).
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's enum rule requires train.Service IN ('Daily'). _apply_enum sets all train.Service values to 'Daily' (rng.choice of a single-element list). However, _plant_nulls runs after _apply_enum and plants NULLs in train.Service (2/29 in feedback). The semantic rule 'Service IN (Daily)' holds under SQL three-valued logic for NULL values (NULL IN ('Daily') is UNKNOWN, not FALSE), so the rule is not violated. This is consistent with the interface NULL rule.
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's table_sizes_per_instance is {station: 12, train: 11, train_station: 11}. choose_table_sizes returns these sizes when all tables are in spec.TABLE_SIZES. The writer appends generated rows to a copy of the compact database. The execution feedback shows rows_added={} (empty), which is a reporting gap: the writer returns {'rows_ok': ok, 'rows_failed': bad} but the CLI's summary hardcodes 'rows_added': {} and 'rows_skipped': {}. This means the actual number of appended rows is not reported in the summary, though the integrity checks (fk_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0, not_ok=0) confirm the rows were written successfully. This is a reporting issue, not a generation error.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: populate 'rows_added' and 'rows_skipped' in the CLI summary from the writer's return value (write_instance_sqlite returns rows_ok/rows_failed but _one discards it). This improves observability but does not block pass.

issues.evidence: The specification's dependencies require train_station.Train_ID -> train.Train_ID and train_station.Station_ID -> station.Station_ID. The program's fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws FK values from the parent's generated values, and _revalidate_fks re-maps any out-of-pool FK values after shaping. The execution feedback shows fk_violations=0 across 20 instances, confirming FK consistency. The writer enables foreign_keys=ON, so any violation would be caught and counted.
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's ties_for_order_limit for station.Annual_interchanges and station.Main_Services requires ties at rank 1 for ASC ordering (no LIMIT). _apply_ties sets cols[c][1] = cols[c][0] for these columns, creating a tie. However, _plant_nulls runs after _apply_ties and may set cols[c][0] or cols[c][1] to NULL, potentially breaking the tie (NULL vs non-NULL). The execution feedback does not report tie verification, so this is an unresolved check. The tie may still hold if both positions are non-NULL or both NULL, but this is not guaranteed.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: verify that ties survive NULL planting, or re-apply ties after _plant_nulls (similar to how _apply_formula is re-applied). This is a minor robustness issue; the tie requirement is a soft target and the execution feedback does not flag it as failed.

issues.evidence: The specification's uncertainty field notes that Location values in the sample include 'Glasgow' not matching station names, treated as independent free text with no correlation to Name. The program's LOCATION_POOL = ['London', 'Birmingham', 'Glasgow'] and NAME_POOL includes 'Glasgow Central'. The program does not enforce any correlation between Location and Name, consistent with the specification's stated uncertainty. This is a documented design choice, not an error.
issues.requested_revision: None required.

issues.evidence: The specification's group_sizes target for station.Number_of_Platforms requires sizes 1, 2, >=3. _shape_group_sizes for INT columns uses base values from the column (or fresh ints) and a plan [g1, g2, g2, g3, g3, g3]. However, _apply_ranges clamps Number_of_Platforms to [1, 200] and runs before _shape_group_sizes. The base values are drawn from the column after range clamping, so they are in [1, 200]. The plan uses base[i%len(base)]+1000+i for rows 6+, which may exceed 200 and be clamped by... wait, _apply_ranges runs before _shape_group_sizes, so the +1000+i values are NOT re-clamped. This means Number_of_Platforms may contain values > 200 (e.g., 1001+), violating the semantic rule Number_of_Platforms > 0 (still holds) but exceeding the RANGES upper bound of 200. The RANGES entry is a program-internal range, not a specification rule; the specification only requires Number_of_Platforms > 0. So this is not a specification violation, but it is an inconsistency between RANGES and the shaping output.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: either re-apply _apply_ranges after _shape_group_sizes, or use a smaller offset in _shape_group_sizes for bounded INT columns. This is a minor consistency issue; the specification's semantic rule (Number_of_Platforms > 0) is not violated.

unresolved_checks: Tie survival after NULL planting for station.Annual_interchanges and station.Main_Services (ties set before _plant_nulls; not verified in execution feedback).

Whether the +1000+i offset in _shape_group_sizes for Number_of_Platforms produces values exceeding the program's RANGES upper bound of 200 (not a specification violation, but an internal inconsistency).
The 'rows_added'/'rows_skipped' fields in the CLI summary are hardcoded empty; actual appended row counts are not reported (integrity checks pass, so rows were written).
reviews.summary: The program ran successfully (20/20 instances, 0 failures, reproducible), with 0 FK violations, 0 NOT NULL violations, 0 PK duplicates, and 0 invalid instances. The specification's semantic rules (Total_Passengers formula, ranges, enum, dependencies) are implemented and supported by evidence. The NULL rule is satisfied for all nullable columns. Group sizes, aggregate counts, ties, duplicates, and unmatched joins are shaped by construction. Minor issues are non-blocking: (1) Total_Passengers boundary planting is superseded by the formula (documented as formula precedence, but the positive literals are also overwritten — should be clarified); (2) ties may not survive NULL planting; (3) Number_of_Platforms shaping may exceed the program's RANGES bound; (4) CLI summary does not report appended row counts. None of these block a pass; the program implements the specification and produces valid, integrity-preserving instances.
